MFA is mandatory on EFTPS: "EFTPS is partnering with third-party credential service providers Login.gov and ID.me for MFA services. Secure sign-in via Login.gov or ID.me is required as of October 19, 2023."

Enrollment ends in physical mail: after IRS validation "you will receive a personal identification number (PIN) via U.S. Mail in five to seven business days" — a hard latency floor no online path removes.
Published scheduling constraint: "Payments using this Web site or our voice response system must be scheduled by 8 p.m. ET the day before the due date to be received timely by the IRS."
The IRS's own EFTPS page: "No new enrollments for individual taxpayers — Individual taxpayers can no longer create new EFTPS accounts." The rail is business and tax-professional only going forward.

The documented software channel is the Batch Provider program, not an API: "If you're a tax professional, you can make payments for multiple clients under a single login. Download the free Batch Provider Software."
Published enrollment clock: "New enrollments for EFTPS can take up to five business days to process."
